findings: src/planner/binder/query_node/plan_select_node.cpp: this is the standard WinMagic unnesting of a correlated MIN/MAX scalar subquery. It refers to no table names, column names, literals or data properties. Every condition is structural: the subquery's scans map to distinct outer scans of the same table, its conjuncts are a subset of the outer conjuncts, and the extra tables attach only through the correlated columns, which must be equality-joined.

Correctness argument checked. Take all outer rows that pass the filter and share the same correlated values. Their subquery-table parts are exactly the rows the subquery aggregates over. Every outer conjunct that touches those tables must match a subquery conjunct, and every unmatched conjunct may reference only the extra tables. So each qualifying subquery row, combined with any extra-table row of the same partition, is itself an outer row. Duplicate rows do not change MIN/MAX. The partition can never be empty, because the outer row itself is in it.

Guards hold up. NULL correlated keys: they must appear as bare column refs in a matched equality, so those outer rows are filtered out either way. Collated VARCHAR: the comparison sides become collation function calls, not bare column refs, so the rewrite does not fire. Floats (-0.0 vs 0.0) and nested types: refused by IsSupportedPartitionType. Casts on the keys, non-equality correlation, depth above 1, volatile expressions, a second subquery, any JOIN/projection/CTE ref/sample node in either tree, table or dynamic filters: all fall back to the existing path.

PlanFilter is only called for the WHERE clause (plan_select_node.cpp:406), so HAVING and QUALIFY are not affected. The window uses the whole partition (UNBOUNDED PRECEDING to UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING, no ORDER BY), which is the semantics this needs.
Minor, not blocking: the change ships no sqllogictest, although the issue planned one for duplicate extra-table keys and NULL keys. The author reports testing these cases by hand.
